newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks set new record close after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks set new record close after U.S. data.

text.p: French shares set a new closing record on Friday, finishing up 0.54 percent, boosted by a rise on Wall Street and U.S. growth data which lowered inflation concern in the U.S.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 13.50 points at 2,516.56 but off an all-time intra day high of 2,521.88.
Traders said profit taking kicked in at the end of the day after the record gains set this week.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up 10 points at 2,519.0.
This week the CAC-40 gained 3.5 percent. Total volume on Friday was 10.9 billion francs. The previous CAC-40 all-time high of 2,505.51 was hit on January 30.
The U.S. data showed that although the U.S. Gross Domestic Product rose much higher than forecast at 4.7 percent, the implicit price deflator was below forecasts at 1.4 percent.
A weaker deflator shows that despite strong economic growth inflation was not getting out of control and lowered chances of a rise in U.S. interest rates.
Dealers linked today's strong volumes to the expiry of the CAC January futures.

Dealers expect the market to consolidate next week after posting strong gains this week and ahead of the meeting of the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee and U.S. January payroll data. "We are heading for a consolidation, at least a pause," one dealer said.
LVMH closed down 3.45 percent at 1,400 francs on disappointment over 1996 sales and a profit warning for 1997 in the wake of the acquisition of U.S. duty-free chain DFS.
Alcatel Alsthom ended up 4.78 percent at 548 francs.
Morgan Stanley has raised its target for Alcatel shares to 650 francs per share from 600 francs.
Alcatel has forecast a spectacular rebound to a profit of 2.5 billion francs for 1996 from a hefty loss of 25.6 billion francs in 1995.
Generale des Eaux finished up 2.61 percent at 708 francs.
Its SGE unit has forecast a sharp reduction in 1996 consolidated loss to 400 million francs.
Saint-Gobain closed up 0.12 percent at 851 francs. Brokerage UBS lowers recommendation to 'sell' from 'hold' after the release of 1996 earnings.
